title: The frontend's transporter page is headed "Search for an approved commercial transporter" but offers no way to search; DR1 puts a search field over name, address and approval number above the list.

controls.text: Search for an approved commercial transporter

finding.frontend: `/transporters/select` carries the h1 "Search for an approved commercial transporter" and, below it, one line of guidance — "Selecting a transporter copies their name, address and approval number into this notification." — and then two radios, the whole commercial-transporter list rendered at once, each option labelled with the transporter's name and hinted with its address and approval number (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.njk:11-23, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:90-93). There is no text input, no search button and no filtering of any kind. The page promises a search and does not have one, and the promise gets less true as the list grows: today two records fit on a screen, and the same page would render two hundred the same way.
finding.prototype: DR1's list page carries a labelled Search field, hinted "Name, address or approval number", directly above the table of transporters (app/views/transporter.html:75-95). Typing filters the rows client-side against a search string built from the record's name, address and approval number. The filter is JavaScript only — the search button is type="button" and the form post reads the search field and then ignores it — so a user without JavaScript gets no filtering.
finding.difference: Add a search input above the transporter list, labelled Search and hinted "Name, address or approval number", filtering the rows on submit. Either that or the heading has to stop saying "Search". This depends on the list page existing in the shape DR1 gives it; it lands with the task-ordering change rather than before it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a search or filter control on `/transporters/select` in the rendered page — the captured DOM has one form, one radios group and no input of type search or text.
finding.correction: CLAIMED: the frontend's page is headed 'Search for an approved commercial transporter' and has no search control, while DR1 puts a search over name, address and approval number above its list. BOTH CONFIRMED FROM THE RENDERED DOM. capture/html/frontend/fe-transporter-commercial.html holds exactly three inputs — a crumb hidden field and two radios named commercialTransporter — and no input of type text or search; the h1 is the search promise verbatim, so the page really does head itself with a thing it does not do. DR1's list page carries label 'Search', hint 'Name, address or approval number' and input name='search' type='search' (app/views/transporter.html:75-96). TWO SMALL CORRECTIONS, both slots amended. The frontend page is not 'nothing but two radios' — it also carries the line 'Selecting a transporter copies their name, address and approval number into this notification.' And DR1's filter does not survive without JavaScript: the POST /transporter handler assigns req.body.search to a local at app/routes.js:10720 and never reads it again, and the search button is type='button'. The difference is still right to ask for a filter that works on submit, but that has to be described as what the frontend needs rather than as copying DR1. HOW CHECKED: extracted every input element from the captured frontend DOM; read the DR1 view and the POST /transporter handler end to end.

relatedTo.why: The search sits on the list page that finding puts first
